claims.claim: The following amounts and match-rate percentages are illustrative, hypothetical scenario outputs used only to demonstrate report shape in the Examples section, not externally sourced facts: a suspicious duplicate charge of 2,450 ILS / 2,450 ש"ח; a 98% match rate with a fuzzy tolerance of 1 ILS / 1 ש"ח and 1.00 ILS / 1.00 ש"ח; a foreign-currency rounding difference of 127.50 ILS / 127.50 ש"ח with a wider 5.00 ILS / 5.00 ש"ח tolerance; a multi-bank case showing 97% and 91% match rates; and 34 missing-invoice transactions totaling 18,200 ILS / 18,200 ש"ח broken into 3,400 ILS / 3,400 ש"ח of office supplies, 5,100 ILS / 5,100 ש"ח of USD software subscriptions, and 9,700 ILS / 9,700 ש"ח of parking and toll charges.

At an 18% VAT rate the VAT portion of a VAT-INCLUSIVE amount is 18/118, i.e. about 15.25% (15.25%) of the gross. So a systematic gap of about 18% against a net figure, or about 15.25% against a gross figure, indicates a VAT-inclusive versus VAT-exclusive mismatch rather than a genuine reconciling item. This is arithmetic derived from the 18% rate, not a separate published figure.

claims.claim: Bank of Israel representative exchange rates are calculated once a day on foreign-currency business days only, so no rate is published on Saturdays, Sundays, Israeli holidays and certain other days. The rate is published after the afternoon sampling window closes, and the Bank of Israel states the rates have no official or legal standing in themselves.
